meta_description:
1,539 likes, 35 comments - wired on October 30, 2026: "In a major blow to both the terminally online and the criminally horny, the fan fiction website Archive of Our Own (AO3) has temporarily shut down due to a “security incident,” according to an update posted on the site.

On October 29, an admin for AO3 posted that the website was “down for maintenance.” The statement said that it could take up to four weeks for service to be fully restored, though it was possible the site would be back up in a “degraded state” sooner, with some of its features disabled.

Though the original statement did not specify the reasons for the closure, subsequent updates said that a “security incident” had taken place, though “we are still in the early stages of response [and] determining its scope.” While the statement said that AO3 did not believe that its user database had been stolen, it urged users to exercise caution and change their passwords for the site.

Run by the Organization for Transformative Works, a nonprofit dedicated to preserving fandom communities on the internet, AO3 was founded in 2007 in part due to concerns about censorship and corporate interests overtaking fandom spaces. The website has 11 million users, according to a 2026 press release, and hosts more than 18 million original works.

Those reliant on AO3 for their daily dose of smut are not taking the news well.

Tap the 🔗 in bio to read the full story.".
